scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: A steel nail sinks instantly, but a steel ship weighing thousands of tonnes floats. How?

scenes.name: displace
scenes.text: When anything goes into water, it pushes some water out of the way. That's called displacement.

scenes.name: archimedes
scenes.text: Archimedes found that the water pushes back up, with a force equal to the weight of water displaced.

scenes.name: shape
scenes.text: A nail displaces only a tiny bit of water. A ship's hull is hollow and wide, so it pushes aside a huge amount.

scenes.name: density
scenes.text: Counting all the air inside, the ship's average density is less than water, so it floats.

scenes.name: load
scenes.text: Add cargo and the ship sinks lower, displacing more water, until it balances again.

scenes.name: plimsoll
scenes.text: Ships have a load line painted on the hull, showing the deepest they can safely sit.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Displace, push back, float. Follow for more on how things really work.
